   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document\n\nThis document covers «DIRECTIVE 2003/87/EC OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 October 2003» the EU Emissions Trading System. It is an EU directive; it applies in the European Union through national law. «in order to promote reductions of greenhouse gas emissions in a cost-effective and economically efficient manner» The text read is «Consolidated TEXT: 32003L0087 — EN — 01.03.2024», a documentation tool.\n\nStatements of what the text requires are marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* where the role of a freight forwarder or a charterer is not named in the text. *Analytical inference:* the date of the next scheduled review is the set of Commission reports in section 6, the earliest being a report on smaller ships due by 31 December 2026.\n\n## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace\n\nThe Directive makes ships, aircraft and installations hold and surrender emission allowances for their verified emissions. For ocean freight the scope is stated in Article 3ga: «shall apply in respect of fifty percent (50 %) of the emissions from ships performing voyages departing from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State and arriving at a port of call outside the jurisdiction of a Member State» and «one hundred percent (100 %) of emissions from ships performing voyages departing from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State and arriving at a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State, and one hundred percent (100 %) of emissions from ships within a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State»\n\nThe effective date for maritime transport is set by the phase-in schedule: «Shipping companies shall be liable to surrender allowances according to the following schedule»\n\nFor a freight forwarder it matters on every ocean leg that touches an EU port and on air legs within the EU, because the shipping company or aircraft operator holds the surrender duty; the source does not state how the allowance cost is passed on, beyond the Article 3gc reimbursement in section 4. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the Directive names the shipping company, aircraft operator or installation operator as the duty holder; no duty on a forwarder is stated, but Article 3gc allows the shipping company to recover cost from another entity (section 4). Effect by cargo vertical (live events, artwork, luxury goods, film and television, automotive, humanitarian) requires carrier-specific data and is not stated by this source.\n\n## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action\n\nMONITORING: no action falls within 30 days of the document date. The nearest dated step that touches ocean freight is «No later than 31 December 2026, the Commission shall present a report to the European Parliament and to the Council in which it shall examine the feasibility and economic, environmental and social impacts of the inclusion in this Directive of emissions from ships, including offshore ships, below 5 000 gross tonnage but not below 400 gross tonnage»\n\n*Operational implication:* an ocean procurement lead lists, before 31 December 2026, the services booked in the last year whose ships are between the two size limits, because the report examines the inclusion of ships in that size band; the text does not say they will be brought into scope.\n\n## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain\n\nThe duty holder for ocean legs is the shipping company. «shipping company’ means the shipowner or any other organisation or person, such as the manager or the bareboat charterer» The Directive then allows the cost to move by contract: «when the ultimate responsibility for the purchase of the fuel, or the operation of the ship, or both, is assumed by an entity other than the shipping company pursuant to a contractual arrangement, the shipping company is entitled to reimbursement from that entity for the costs arising from the surrender of allowances» «The shipping company shall remain the entity responsible for surrendering allowances as required under Articles 3gb and 12 and for overall compliance with the provisions of national law transposing this Directive.»\n\nA freight forwarder is not named. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder that books space or charters a vessel is an entity that has assumed responsibility for the purchase of the fuel or the operation of the ship is a threshold question set out in section 7.\n\n## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events\n\nSeveral dated Commission steps follow. The size report is in section 3. «No later than 30 September 2028, the Commission shall assess the appropriateness of extending the application of Article 3ga(3), second subparagraph, beyond 31 December 2030 and, if appropriate, submit a legislative proposal to that effect.» The consequence the text gives is a possible legislative proposal. For the allowances reserved for eligible aviation fuels: «By 1 January 2028, the Commission shall carry out an evaluation regarding the application of this paragraph and submit the results of that evaluation in a report» The text adds: «The report may, where appropriate, be accompanied by a legislative proposal to allocate a capped and time- limited amount of allowances until 31 December 2034»\n\nThe supply of allowances narrows on a fixed path, «The linear factor shall be 4,3 % from 2024 to 2027 and 4,4 % from 2028.» and the next published quantity is «By 30 June 2027, the Commission shall publish the Union-wide quantity of allowances for 2028 and, if required, the adjusted linear reduction factor.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the linear factor rises from 4,3 % to 4,4 % from 2028, so the Union-wide quantity of allowances falls faster from that year; the sources give no price effect.\n\n## 7. Threshold Questions\n\nOne threshold question decides whether a party other than the shipping company can be asked to pay: what counts as taking over the operation of the ship. The text defines it: «‘Operation of the ship’ for the purposes of this Article means determining the cargo carried or the route and the speed of the ship.»\n\n*Legal Confirmation Required:* the text does not apply the definition to a forwarder, so whether a forwarder, or a party that charters a ship, determines the cargo carried or the route and the speed of the ship is not decided here and should be confirmed with counsel before a contract clause is written.\n\n## 8. Substantive Requirements\n\nThe substantive requirement is to hold and surrender allowances for verified emissions, with a penalty if not.\n\n- Surrender: «(c) each shipping company surrenders a number of allowances that is equal to its total emissions during the preceding calendar year, as verified in accordance with Article 3ge.»\n- Maritime phase-in: «(a) 40 % of verified emissions reported for 2024 that would be subject to surrender requirements in accordance with Article 12; (b) 70 % of verified emissions reported for 2025 that would be subject to surrender requirements in accordance with Article 12; (c) 100 % of verified emissions reported for 2026 and each year thereafter»\n- Derogation for ice-class ships only: «By way of derogation from paragraph 3, first subparagraph, point (c), shipping companies may surrender 5 % fewer allowances than their verified emissions released until 31 December 2030 from ice-class ships, provided that such ships have the ice class IA or IA Super or an equivalent ice class»\n- Penalty: «The excess emissions penalty shall be EUR 100 for each tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent emitted for which the operator or aircraft operator has not surrendered allowances.» «The penalties set out in paragraph 3 shall also apply in respect of shipping companies.»\n- Indexation: «The excess emissions penalty relating to allowances issued from 1 January 2013 onwards shall increase in accordance with the European index of consumer prices.»\n- Support for eligible aviation fuels: «(a) 70 % of the remaining price differential between the use of fossil kerosene and hydrogen from renewable energy sources, and advanced biofuels» «(b) 95 % of the remaining price differential between the use of fossil kerosene and renewable fuels of non-biological origin compliant with Article 25 of Directive (EU) 2018/2001, used in aviation»\n- Border adjustment: «From 2034, no CBAM factor shall apply.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the excess emissions penalty of EUR 100 applies to each tonne for which allowances were not surrendered and rises with consumer prices; the phase-in to 100 % for 2026 means the surrender duty covers all verified emissions reported for 2026 and after, against 40 % for 2024 and 70 % for 2025; the source does not state how that cost is passed on.\n\n*Legal Confirmation Required:* the surrender duty, the maritime phase-in and the excess emissions penalty bind the shipping company; whether a party that charters a vessel and determines its cargo or route has assumed the operation of the ship under Article 3gc, and so bears the surrender cost by contract, is a question for counsel.\n\nNo phase-in is stated for aviation outside the dated steps above. No exceptions are stated in Article 16(3). No scope limits are stated in Article 16(3) beyond the operators, aircraft operators and shipping companies it names.\n\nObligations surveyed: 9; workspace-adjacent: 7; extracted as FACT: 9.\n\n## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations\n\nThe reporting duties sit with shipping companies and administering authorities: «the administering authority in respect of a shipping company shall ensure that a shipping company under its responsibility monitors and reports the relevant parameters during a reporting period»\n\n*Legal Confirmation Required:* the text sets no registration or reporting duty for a freight forwarder; whether a party that takes over operation under Article 3gc inherits any data duty is not stated.\n\n## 11. Operational System Requirements\n\nMONITORING: the operational system requirement for a forwarder is a quote field and a contract clause.\n\n- An ocean pricing lead records, at the next quote run, whether each shipping company states an allowance charge, with the allowance price and date it states.\n- A contract lead asks counsel, before the next contractual arrangement with a shipping company is signed, whether it should say who bears the cost under Article 3gc.\n\n*Operational implication:* both steps use only the provisions quoted and no allowance price.\n\n## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline\n\n- 13 October 2003: the Directive is adopted\n- 1 January 2013: the penalty indexation begins for allowances issued from this date\n- 2024: maritime transport enters with 40 % of verified emissions\n- 2025: 70 % of verified emissions\n- 2026: 100 % of verified emissions\n- 31 December 2026: Commission report on smaller ships\n- 30 June 2027: Commission publishes the Union-wide quantity of allowances for 2028\n- 1 January 2028: Commission evaluation report\n- 2028: the linear factor rises to 4,4 %\n- 30 September 2028: Commission assesses extending Article 3ga(3)\n- 2034: no CBAM factor applies\n\n## 15. Sources\n\n- eur-lex.europa.eu: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32003L0087\n- eur-lex.europa.eu: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02003L0087-20240301\n- eur-lex.europa.eu: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:02003L0087-20230605",

Expected Trajectory and Conversion Triggers\n\nThe conversion trigger in the source is the recovery of Middle East oil production, which the agency expects to pull prices down. «As oil production in the Middle East rises, we expect crude oil prices to fall, dropping to an average of $89/b in 4Q26 and $79/b in 2027.» The outlook was issued in the form «Release Date: May 12, 2026  |  Forecast Completed: May 7, 2026» so its path is a forecast from that date, not an observed price.\n\n- May 12, 2026: the agency issues its May outlook, expecting Brent around $106 per barrel in May and June; both months have passed and the pages hold no observed Brent price for them\n- 2027: the agency expects an average of $79 per barrel\n\n*Analytical inference:* the forecast path is downward, but it depends on Middle East production rising and the Strait of Hormuz flows recovering; the source gives no date for that recovery.\n\n## 4.    "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document\n\nThis document covers «COMMISSION DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) 2025/656 of 2 April 2025 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards standards for wireless recharging, electric road system, vehicle-to-grid communication and hydrogen supply for road transport vehicles» It is an EU instrument and applies in the European Union. «Official Journal of the European Union EN L series 2025/656 18.6.2025»\n\nThe delegated act exists because «The Commission may amend Annex II on technical specifications of Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 to introduce new technical specifications or update references to the standards set out in that Annex to enable full technical interoperability of the recharging and refuelling infrastructure in terms of physical connections, communication exchanges and access for persons with reduced mobility.»\n\nStatements of what the text requires are marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* where the role of a freight forwarder is not named in the text; statements that go beyond the text are marked as analysis.\n\n## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace\n\nThe Regulation changes the technical standards that recharging points must meet under Regulation (EU) 2023/1804. «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 8 January 2026.» «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* for a freight forwarder that sells road legs, the connector and communication standards (claims 5 and 9) bear on which public charging points a truck can use; the source states no effect on a forwarder. The connector rule reads: «Direct current (DC) high-power recharging points for recharging infrastructure capable of supplying electricity to both light- and heavy-duty electric vehicles shall be equipped, for interoperability purposes, at least with vehicle connectors of the combined charging system “Combo 2” for Mode 4 recharging as described in standard EN IEC 62196-3:2022.»\n\n*Legal Confirmation Required:* the text sets standards for recharging points; it names no duty on a freight forwarder, and the source states no effect on a forwarder. Effect by cargo vertical (live events, artwork, luxury goods, film and television, automotive, humanitarian) requires carrier-specific data and is not stated by this source.\n\n## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action\n\nMONITORING: no action falls within 30 days of the document date; the nearest dated change is a standard that applies to newly installed or renovated points from 1 January 2027. «Publicly accessible recharging points for alternating current (AC) and direct current (DC) for light- and heavy-duty electric vehicles installed or renovated from 1 January 2027 shall comply, for interoperability purposes, at least with standard EN ISO 15118-20:2022»\n\n*Operational implication:* a procurement lead who tenders road legs that rely on public heavy-duty charging asks each road carrier at the next tender to record the installation or renovation date of the public heavy-duty charging points it relies on, so that points installed or renovated from 1 January 2027 can be checked against the newer standard; the decision that changes on 1 January 2027 is which standard applies to newly installed or renovated points.\n\n## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain\n\nThe compliance chain in the text runs through the people who build and run recharging points. «Operators and manufacturers of both publicly accessible and private recharging points specifically for Mode 3 and 4 recharging for electric vehicles»\n\nA freight forwarder is not named in the text. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder that owns or operates its own depot charging is an operator in the sense of the text is not stated and should be confirmed with counsel; the source states no effect on a forwarder that buys road legs.\n\n## 8. Substantive Requirements\n\nThe substantive requirements are technical standards set by date of installation or renovation.\n\n- Definitions: «“installed” means the initial placement of all relevant recharging point equipment, including hardware, software and associated electrical infrastructure, such as electricity supply connections, transformers, and other electrical systems, to enable the recharging of electric vehicles; (b) “renovated” means a major or complete replacement of relevant recharging point equipment.»\n- Buses and connectors from 8 January 2026: «alternating current (AC) normal-power recharging points and high-power recharging points for electric buses that are installed or renovated from 8 January 2026 shall be equipped, for interoperability purposes, at least with connectors of Type 2 for Mode 3 recharging as described in standard EN IEC 62196-2:2022;»\n- Vehicle-to-grid communication for public points from 8 January 2026: «The publicly accessible recharging points for alternating current (AC) and direct current (DC) for light- and heavy-duty electric vehicles installed or renovated from 8 January 2026 shall comply, for interoperability purposes, at least with the following standards»\n- Existing equipment: «direct current (DC) normal-power recharging points installed before that date shall continue to comply with standard EN IEC 62196-3:2014 until they are renovated»\n- Private points from 1 January 2027: «Private recharging points for alternating current (AC) and direct current (DC) electric light- and heavy-duty electric vehicles installed or renovated from 1 January 2027 shall comply, for interoperability purposes, at least with the following standards»\n- Scope extensions: «Technical specifications for electric road system (ERS) for dynamic ground-level power supply through conductive rails for light- and heavy-duty electric vehicles»\n- Private points by recharging mode: «(a) EN IEC 61851-1:2019 “Electric vehicle conductive charging system – Part 1: General requirements” (for Mode 2 recharging); (b) EN ISO 15118-20:2022 “Road vehicles – Vehicle to grid communication interface – Part 20: 2nd generation network layer and application layer requirements” (for Mode 3 or Mode 4 recharging)»\n\n*Analytical inference:* for a forwarder the practical content is a split in time: points installed or renovated from 8 January 2026 follow one standard set, public points and private Mode 3 or Mode 4 points installed or renovated from 1 January 2027 a newer one (private Mode 2 points follow EN IEC 61851-1:2019), and direct current normal-power points installed before that date continue to comply with standard EN IEC 62196-3:2014 until they are renovated.\n\n*Legal Confirmation Required:* the connector, vehicle-to-grid and private-point standards bind recharging points by their installation or renovation date; whether a forwarder's own depot charging counts as a private recharging point under these provisions, and whether a given equipment replacement counts as renovated, are questions for counsel.\n\nNo phase-in is stated in Articles 1 and 2 beyond the dates above. No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 and 2. No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 and 2 other than the installed-or-renovated dates.\n\nObligations surveyed: 6; workspace-adjacent: 3; extracted as FACT: 7.\n\n## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations\n\nThe text sets no registration or reporting obligation for freight forwarders. It states technical standards for recharging points and no filing, notification or reporting duty in Articles 1 and 2. The penalty summary is a gap: the captured text states no penalty or sanction. *Legal Confirmation Required:* reporting duties under Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 are outside the captured text and are not covered here.\n\n## 11. Operational System Requirements\n\nMONITORING: the operational system requirement for a forwarder is a data field, not a system change.\n\n- A procurement lead adds, at the next carrier onboarding round or tender, a field to the road carrier onboarding form recording whether the carrier's public heavy-duty charging was installed or renovated from 1 January 2027, and which vehicle-to-grid standard it supports.\n- A tender owner adds the same question to any tender that names a charging-dependent lane.\n\n*Operational implication:* these two steps use only the dates the text states and no cost figure.\n\n## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline\n\n- 2 April 2025: the Regulation is adopted (\"Done at Brussels, 2 April 2025\")\n- 18 June 2025: the Regulation is published in the Official Journal\n- 8 January 2026: the Regulation begins to apply, and points installed or renovated from this date follow the standards in Annex II as replaced\n- 1 January 2027: the newer vehicle-to-grid standard is the standard for points installed or renovated from this date\n\n## 15.
